newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee set to go on line Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee set to go on line Tuesday.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant was prepared to go back on line after a six-week shutdown to investigate safety concerns, a plant official said Tuesday.

The facility was expected to be generating electricity by the end of Tuesday while investigation continues into how 15 feet of wire was removed from an electrical circuit in a key cooling system, spokesman Leanne Deihl said.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
The 24-year-old plant on the Maine coast was taken out of operation July 19, when engineers discovered a potential design defects in the containment core coolingand instrumentation systems.

An attempt to restart the 910-megawatt plant in late August was aborted when plant officials discovered that a wire had been removed from the circuit that would automatically start pumps in the emergency core cooling system.

Maine Yankee has been limited to 90 percent capacity while the Nuclear Regulatory Commission investigates allegations engineers improperly manipulated computer testing of the emergency core cooling system in the 1980s.
Plant officials have denied wrongdoing, but submitted new tests to the NRC using a difference computer model.
